nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty title
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Sort Tasks Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

# Review documents: Twilio

**Pattern:** Approval Workflow · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers standups work end to end across Twilio and Notion.

It moves through 12 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Task Form Submission
2. Normalize Task Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'auto-approve' → Notion
5. Fast-Track 'needs-review' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Stamp Processing Time
9. Guard Non-Empty title
10. Sort Tasks Newest First
11. Cap Batch Volume
12. Send Summary to Twilio

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing standups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Task Form Submission → Normalize Task Payload → Route by Work Type → Process 'auto-approve' → Notion → Fast-Track 'needs-review' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty title → Sort Tasks Newest First → Cap Batch Volume → Send Summary to Twilio → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Twilio and Notion aligned by hand for standups
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Twilio, for standups
- Standups work where "Normalize Task Payload" is still a manual step before Twilio
- Standups work that only reaches Twilio when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Twilio and Notion in step for standups, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Twilio or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 14 nodes in this standups build
- Branches rejoin before Twilio, so a standups run reports once rather than 14 times
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 14 nodes for standups before wiring Twilio
- 14 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for standups

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Notion integration token; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

Once it's wired up with real credentials, try:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your standups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole standups payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
